outcome_classes.description: Returns a list of tickets matching the given queue and status filters.
Returns an empty array when no ticket matches the filters; observed directly in a trace call (queue=shipping, status=open) that returned [].
query_tickets never errors on a read: every call, including find_tickets, returns a value and nothing about a lookup raises partway through -- so there is no error path for find_tickets to enumerate.

No claim addresses whether find_tickets can ever signal a distinct 'not found' outcome apart from returning an empty array. Because it is a filtered list read rather than a lookup of one target, and its queue/status parameters are restricted to a closed enum, nothing in the claim set says whether some filter state could produce a distinct not-found signal instead of an empty list.
Returns one ticket together with its comments, ordered by position.

No claim states what get_ticket returns for a ticket that exists but has zero comments. The Ticket/Comment entity claims permit comment_count to be 0, but nothing says whether the response shape differs (e.g. an empty comments array) in that case.

The claim set disagrees on what happens when get_ticket is called with an id no ticket has. notes.md's clm-notes-md-007 states this is an error, while notes.md's own clm-notes-md-008 states query_tickets never errors on a read and that nothing about a lookup raises partway through, and an independent trace (clm-trace-json-003) shows one captured get_ticket call with an unknown id returning an empty object rather than raising. Which behavior actually occurs is unresolved -- see the recorded contradictions.

No claim addresses what happens when get_ticket is called with a missing or non-integer ticket_id, as opposed to a well-formed integer id that has no ticket. clm-api-json-002 only requires 'action', and clm-api-json-006 only states ticket_id's type, without describing invocation-time validation behavior.

invariants.statement: comment_count on a ticket is always the number of comment records attached to it; the field is recomputed on read, so a stored value that disagrees is overwritten.
ticket_id is unique across every queue, not merely unique within a single queue.

Inferred: queue is constrained to "billing" or "shipping", combining query_tickets' queue parameter enum (clm-api-json-004) with notes.md's statement that ticketq fronts exactly those two support queues (clm-notes-md-001). This is a value-membership constraint, not one of the four machine forms, so it is recorded as prose.

Inferred: status is constrained to "open", "blocked", or "closed", per query_tickets' status parameter enum (clm-api-json-005). No claim states this as a stored-data rule directly, only as the parameter's accepted values, so it is recorded as prose rather than promoted to machine.

goals.statement: Find the ticket in a queue that still needs the engineer's attention, via a single lookup.
Explain why a ticket is stuck: find the ticket, then read its comments to find where the blocker is named.

contradictions.nature: clm-notes-md-007 states that calling get_ticket with an id no ticket has is an error; clm-trace-json-003 is an independent, captured call to get_ticket with an unknown id (9999) that returned an empty object rather than raising.
contradictions.rationale: Exactly one claim states the error behavior and exactly one independent artifact shows the empty-object behavior; nothing else in the claim set breaks the tie between a stated design rule and a single captured example. This is the shape the toy fixture's own guidance warns about: with corroboration removed on both sides, one claim each, the only honest resolution is unresolved -- not a guess about which is more typical of an API like this.

contradictions.nature: Within notes.md itself, clm-notes-md-007 states get_ticket on an unknown id is an error, while clm-notes-md-008 states query_tickets never errors on a read and that nothing about a lookup raises partway through -- a general statement that, read plainly, would cover get_ticket on an unknown id and directly contradicts clm-notes-md-007.
contradictions.rationale: Both statements come from the same document; the claim set gives no way to tell which the author intended as authoritative for the not-found case specifically. clm-trace-json-003's observed empty-object return is consistent with clm-notes-md-008's general reading, but a single captured trace call is not independent, tie-breaking corroboration for treating 008 as authoritative over 007 -- doing so would rest on '008 is the general rule plus one matching example, so it must be right,' which is the same convention-standing-in-for-evidence reasoning this stage is supposed to refuse rather than reach for.

gaps.subject: get_ticket's response shape for a ticket with zero comments
gaps.unknown: Whether or how the get_ticket response differs (e.g. an empty comments array vs. some other shape) when a ticket exists but has no attached comments.
gaps.why_it_matters: rb-propose needs this to write a sound gold answer for any get_ticket scenario targeting a comment-less ticket; inventing the shape would inject an unstated fact into every scenario built on it.

gaps.subject: get_ticket's behavior on a missing or non-integer ticket_id
gaps.unknown: Whether an invocation with a missing or wrongly-typed ticket_id is rejected as an error, coerced, or handled some other way, as distinct from a well-formed integer id that simply has no ticket.
gaps.why_it_matters: rb-propose and rb-challenge both need this to design or perturb get_ticket scenarios around malformed input without inventing the target's actual validation behavior.

gaps.subject: Whether find_tickets has any 'not found' outcome distinct from an empty result list
gaps.unknown: No claim addresses whether some filter state could produce a distinct not-found or invalid-filter signal from find_tickets, as opposed to an empty array.
gaps.why_it_matters: rb-propose needs this before it can soundly claim a find_tickets scenario is exercising a 'not found' path rather than merely an 'empty results' path.
